newsitem.title: UK: UK's FTSE 100 stays firm, market remains cautious.
newsitem.headline: UK's FTSE 100 stays firm, market remains cautious.

text.p: ** FTSE 100 stays moderately higher but volume remains light
as many investors fret about interest rates and politics.
** Strong banks, oils, and pharmaceuticals bolster FTSE.
** FTSE near-term upside seen capped around 4,355 resistance

Trading volume was 395 million shares, a figure once again inflated by heavy turnover in Alliance & Leicester Plc which made its market debut on Monday. Declining issues pipped advancers by 50 to 45, with five FTSE 100 constituents unchanged.

Fears of higher interest rates spooked Wall Street on Monday, sending the Dow Industrials Average 43 points lower. Growing fears that the next British government will hike UK base rates soon after the May 1 ballot, weighed on investor sentiment on this side of the Atlantic, dealers said.
"The market has already discounted at least a 25 basis point hike next month. But if we get 50 basis points, there could be a bit of panic," another trader said.
Barclays Bank Plc was up 8p to 10.36-1/2 stg, after the company told its annual meeting it had made a good start to 1997, with an encouraging first quarter for its investment banking arm, BZW.
Shares in Alliance & Leicester Plc, which made a sparkling market debut on Monday, fell 27-1/2 to 539, in volume of around 62 million shares, representing 16 percent of total market turnover.

Better-than-expected earnings statements on Monday from U.S. oil groups Exxon Corp and Amoco Corp lifted Shell Transport and Trading Plc 14-1/2p to 10.66 stg, while British Petroleum Plc added 4-1/2p to 696.

Amongst drug stocks, SmithKline Beecham Plc was up 21p to 927 after the company hailed its underlying growth in sales and profits as "excellent", despite the strong pound which had adversely impacted on overall earnings.
SmithKline reported an eight percent rise in Q1 profit despite a "dramatic" impact from sterling, which has risen over 20 percent against major European currencies since last summer.
Elsewhere in the sector, Glaxo Holdings Plc was up 12-1/2p to 11.63 stg, while Zeneca Plc jumped 25p to 18.64-1/2 stg.
Reckitt and Colman Plc bounced 14p to 821-1/2p, after NatWest Securities said it was advising clients to add to their Reckitt holdings.
Furniture maker DFS rose 15p to 547-1/2, after the company reported first-half pre-tax profits of 18.7 million stg, ahead of expectations, and said it was confident of continued growth and success.
